newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh cuts restrictions to lure investment.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh cuts restrictions to lure investment.

text.p: Bangladesh, desperately seeking rapid industrialisation, said on Tuesday investors wishing to set up a company in the country were no longer required to declare their income sources to authorities.
Officials said a cabinet meeting on Monday approved a proposal that would allow the unrestricted inflow of funds to prop up investment.
"This means nobody is going to ask your source of income and whether you have paid any income tax for such earnings," one official said.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina presided over the meeting which endorsed the new policy aimed to channel "undeclared" money towards industrial investment.
Earlier, investors needed to declare their source of investment capital to the tax authorities.
The new facility would be in effect for three years from January 1997, officials said.
Bangladesh is striving to raise the rate of investment to more than 20 percent of its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) from the current 17 percent.
Government officials admitted that huge amounts of funds were lying idle because the earners had evaded tax or refused to divulge their sources of income.
"This is a test case. We are compromising the issue of morality only to lure black money (undeclared money) into productive investment," said one official with the government's revenue board.
The official could not give an estimate of the amount of "black money" in the country.
